text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
JOHN BATMAN was born on this day in 1801. He founded the site for Melbourne, saying it was "a good spot for a village".
Polish naturalist WILLIAM BLANDOWSKI was born in 1822. In Australia he faced dispute, but still named 19 species of fish after Council Members of the Melbourne Philosophical Society.
The American General who commanded Confederate forces in the Civil War, THOMAS "STONEWALL" JACKSON, was born in 1824.
Australian cricketer (batsman) HERBERT COLLINS was born in 1889. He had several nicknames including "MAULDY", "NUTTY" and "BERT", but to his bookmakers he was known as "HORSESHOE" or "LUCKY".
Australian soldier LAWRENCE McCARTHY was born in 1892. He won the Victoria Cross in 1918, when he killed 20 Germans and took 50 prisoners single-handed.
French fashion designer CHRISTIAN DIOR was born on this day in 1905.

American film actor, best known for his television role as "KOJAK", TELLY SAVALAS, was born in 1925. The baldheaded film and television star had a single hit with a spoken version of 'Bread's' "It" (1975). His acting career began at the relatively late age of 40. He played "KOJAK" from 1973 to 1978.
Australian Olympic athlete RON CLARKE was born in 1937.
Legendary American golfer JACK NIKLAUS was born on this day in 1940.
Spanish opera tenor PLACIDO DOMINGO was born in 1941.

American singer/songwriter MAC DAVIS was born in 1941. Success only came after other artists recorded his songs. These included LOU RAWLS with "You're Good For Me", GLEN CAMPBELL with "Within My Memory" and ELVIS PRESLEY with "In The Ghetto" and "Don't Cry Daddy". In his solo career he had hits with "Baby Don't Get Hooked On Me" (1972) and "Stop And Smell The Roses" (1974). MAC had his own television show in the United States from 1974 to 1976 and starred in several films.

Trinidad-born singer/songwriter BILLY OCEAN (LESLIE SEBASTIAN CHARLES) was born in 1950. His hits included "Loverboy" (1984), "Suddenly" (1985), "When The Going Gets Tough, The Tough Get Going" (1985) and "Get Outta My Dreams, Get Into My Car" (1988).
** EVENTS **
1648 : The first woman lawyer in the American colonies,
MARGARET BRENT, was denied the right to vote. She was a wealthy land-owner, and challenged a poll that had been conducted in her absence.
1790 : Dr JOSEPH GUILLOTIN demonstrated his new execution
device, whereby a heavy blade drops from a frame and beheads the victim.
1973 : France's KING LOUIS XVI died on the guillotine,
after being found guilty of treason.
1846 : The first edition of the "DAILY NEWS", edited by
CHARLES DICKENS, was published in London.
1899 : Britain's Lord KITCHENER was appointed the
Governor-General of Sudan.
1901 : ELISHA GRAY, U.S. inventor who contested the first
patent for the telephone with ALEXANDER GRAHAM BELL, died.
1907 : Taxi cabs were officially recognised in Britain.
1908 : A law was passed in the New York City, making it
illegal for women to smoke in public.
1911 : The first Monte Carlo car rally was staged.
1924 : The "Father of the Russian Revolution", VLADIMIR
ILYICH LENIN, died at the age of 53.
1930 : The first "BUCK ROGERS" comic strip was published
in the United States.
1950 : Author GEORGE ORWELL (ANIMAL FARM, 1984), best
known for the quote "all animals are equal but some are more equal than others", died.
1951 : Atomic bombs were first tested in the American
State of Nevada.
1954 : The United States launched its first nuclear
submarine "NAUTILUS".
1959 : Death of CECIL B. De MILLE, American film producer
best known for his biblical epics.
1976 : British and French Concordes made their first
commercial flights.
1986 : Women's one piece bathing suits were outselling
bikinis.
1988 : Briton BRIAN MILTON landed his microlight aircraft
in Darwin, following a 51-day flight from London.
1994 : Belgian Deputy Prime Minister GUY COEME and two
other eading Socialist politicians resigned over a bribery scandal.
